title: Max Roach and Dave Tough on a cold Chicago street
summary: Freeman recalls meeting Max Roach in the Chicago wind and talking for 35 minutes about Dave Tough, who he says influenced avant-garde drummers.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, if it's all right, let's go back to Dave again. Davey. Because I would like -- well first of all, on the subject of Davey, I mean people like Chick, I mean drummers that appreciated Davey so much and this was in the days before white drummers were really drumming.
Well, what I was going to say before
and I got off the track, but I knew we would get back to it and you have just taken me back to it.

I remember running into Max Roach who we'd say is the father or grandfather, so-called of avant garde drumming and I don't, although Max himself wouldn't use that category, but that's what the critics called him.

Yes. I ran into Max. I had never seen him before nor had he ever seen me, but we had seen each other's pictures. And it was a cold February day in Chicago and I was playing the Blue Note, and I think Max was playing at the London House, and the wind was up about near the north side of so 45 miles an hour, Michigan Avenue, and we were both -- he was coming -- he was walking south and I was walking north going our different ways, of course, and we were really, you know, holding our coats, because it was terribly cold, Alaskan weather, in February, he looked at me and he said, 'Bud Freeman,' and I said, 'Max Roach,' and we got into a doorway somewhere and what do you think we talked about: in that cold for 35 minutes. Dave Tough.
Max told me how much he admired Dave and how the ideas he got...
Yes, Dave died in 1948, didn't he?
I think That would be the year, and there
were Max and I talking about Dave for 35 minutes and just a marvelous -- too bad all the avant-garde other drummers who copied Max didn't know that they were really copying Dave Tough.
Well, no, he didn't say that in those words, but I know how influenced he was by Dave Tough.
Oh, no doubt about it, and Max and I on the strength of that, have been very good friends since. I ran into him in Italy a couple of years ago. Nice guy.
